title: Set a soda can in a seat-back fold-down cup holder: fold down its tray, swing out its ring, set the can in upright
instruction: Put the soda can in the seat-back cup holder: fold down its tray, swing out its ring, set the can upright through the ring onto the tray, and let go.
context: Most people have set a drink in a fold-down cup holder: on the back of a car or van seat, in a minivan door, or on a cinema or stadium seat. North American cinemas alone sold about 760 to 780 million tickets in 2025. The US fleet is about 289 million light vehicles (2025). This holder stows flat: its tray stands folded up over its ring. A hand folds the tray down to its stop, then swings the ring up and out to its stop, and a full 12 oz can is lowered through a ring only about 4 mm wider than the can until it stands on the tray. A can lowered at an angle catches the rim and tips; one let go above the ring drops onto the tray. The task ends with both parts open and the can standing upright on the tray inside the ring, both hands clear.
setup: Metres; x forward, y to the robot's left, z up; origin midway between the arm bases (0, +/-0.305); heights above the bench top. (1) Seat-back panel section, fixed: a rigid upholstered-look board 0.45 wide (y) x 0.40 tall x 0.05 thick, standing on the bench, its face at x = 0.360, centred on y = 0 (estimate of a seat back's lower section; a real holder sits 0.6 to 0.7 above the floor, lowered here to bench height for reach, at true scale). (2) A Sea-Dog 588210-1 fold-up drink holder (sea-dog.com/groups/1055-flush-mount-drink-holder; wholesalemarine.com/sea-dog-abs-folding-drink-holder), black ABS, true size, screwed to the panel's face: a 98 x 95 x 4 mm plate (drawing B 3-7/8 in, A 3-3/4 in) with two folding parts on their own pivots. A ring, 70 mm inside (C: holds drinks up to 2-3/4 in) and 80 mm outside, band 8 mm tall, on two side arms pivoted along y at the plate's top corners (pivot line at x = 0.347, 0.16 up). A tray, 72 deep x 84 wide, 3 mm floor and 7 mm lips on its front and sides, hinged along y at the plate's bottom (hinge line at x = 0.339, 0.076 up). Both start stowed: the ring hanging flat 1 mm in front of the plate, the tray folded up over it, 24 mm deep in all from the panel face (E 15/16 in). Open, each stands level at a hard stop: the ring's centre at (0.305, 0), its top face 0.16 up, 84 mm over the tray floor, its front 95 mm from the panel face (D 3-7/16 in, 87 mm). No spring or detent; joint damping (0.05 N m s/rad, estimate) holds each where it is put. (3) A 12 oz / 355 ml aluminium soda can, 66 mm x 122.2 mm, 0.37 kg, free, rigid, standing on a 10 cm square mat, 2 mm thick, centred at (0.22, -0.17). Both arms start at their ready pose, grippers open. Reset: lift the can out and back onto its mat, fold the ring down and the tray up; about 30 s. Real trial: the same Sea-Dog 588210-1 screwed to an upright board, a phone level app laid on the can's top after the trial, a phone filming the side.
scoring: Read from the state at the end; only the voids latch. 0.33: the tray and the ring each within 10 degrees of fully open. 0.67: also the can inside the ring, its axis within 10 degrees of vertical and of the ring's axis, crossing the ring's top face within 3 mm of its centre, its base 3 mm or more below that face. 1.0: also its base within 2 mm of the tray floor, the can still (under 0.01 m/s and 0.1 rad/s), every part of both grippers 50 mm or more from the can and the holder, for 2 s running. Void (0): once off its mat (its base risen over 10 mm), the can tilts past 30 degrees, or moves down faster than 0.3 m/s (a free fall of about 5 mm) while no hand holds it. A hand holds it while its jaws are open no more than 1 mm a side past the can (68 mm across), a point of each finger is within 8 mm of the can, and it slips down under 0.1 m/s relative to the hand; a held descent at any speed does not void. Real trial: both parts against their stops, the can's base on the tray floor, both grippers 5 cm or more from the can and holder with nothing touching the can for 2 s, and after the trial a phone level app laid on the can's top reads under 10 degrees. Void: the can tips past 30 degrees once off its mat, or falls free more than about 5 mm at any time once off its mat (fingers open or it slips out of the hand); both judged in the side film, the fall against a tape mark on the board.
fidelity: Sizes from the Sea-Dog 588210-1 drawing (A, B, C, E) and listing; band, lip and arm lengths are estimates from its photo, the open ring 8 mm farther out than D. Ring and tray are links with hard stops, no spring or detent (none published); damping holds each where put, weight left out. The stowed tray blocks the ring; neither hits the plate. Ring 1 mm off the plate, as real. Play: 2 mm a side on the real holder, about 1.3 in the model (16-flat ring), tighter. Can: one rigid body.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 (hit the 1,200-step limit). Demo: 1.0 (both arms, 914 steps, 45.7 s, GPU). One arm alone 1.0; holder opened only 0.33; ring before tray 0 (blocked); can kept hold of 0.67; can on the bench beside 0.33; let go 35 mm over the ring 0 (drop); held can brought down fast 1.0; nothing 0.
